# Packet — hammurabi-epilogue-3: Epilogue III — the curses of Ea, Šamaš, Sin and Adad

Stele Col. xlii 98 – xliii 80 — 85 lines of Harper's transliteration (pp. 104–106).

## Where the signs are
Harper's autograph plates in source/harper1904-cornell.pdf (render with pymupdf at 200–300 dpi and read them):

- Plate 76 = PDF page 367 (columns XLI, XLII)
- Plate 77 = PDF page 369 (columns XLII)
- Plate 78 = PDF page 371 (columns XLII, XLIII)
- Plate 79 = PDF page 373 (columns XLIII)
- Plate 80 = PDF page 375 (columns XLIII, XLIV)
- Harper's List of Signs: PDF pages 381–411

## Harper's transliteration, line by line (col · line · text)
Raised text in braces: {b}, {ilu} = the divine determinative (write it {d} with the AN sign, role det), {amêlu} = the LÚ determinative, {kam}. Harper writes many logograms as the Akkadian word (eḳlam for A.ŠÀ) — the plate decides the sign. ḳ = q.

## Notes from the transcription (apparatus)

- Col. XLII 5–9 and XLIII 70–74 (Epilogue): Harper's print shows only four line-dividers' worth of text for five stele lines; the provisional numbering is flagged on the lines concerned.
- Words split across Harper's page turns were joined: XVII 60 tamka-rum, XIX 47 i-du-uk-ku, XXIX 73, XXX 65 iš-ru-ḳu-ši-im, XLII 56, XLIV 35.
- COUNT MISMATCH XLII 5–9: between numerals 5 and 10 there are only 4 bar-segments (i-gul-ma | di-ni la u-{b}ša-az-zi-iḳ | a-wa-ti-ia la uš-te-pi-el | u-zu-ra-ti-ia). Numbered 5–8 and line 9 left absent; a bar is probably missing in Harper's print (perhaps within 'a-wa-ti-ia la uš-te-pi-el'). Needs a human ruling.
- XLII 56: 'la ut-ta-ka-' at the foot of the page and '-ru' at the top of Cornell 124; joined here as la ut-ta-ka-ru. The Cornell 124 file starts at XLII 57.
- Broken type read as the obvious letter: XLII 2 'šnm-ma' read šum-ma; XLII 27 'di-iu' read di-in; XLII 47 'na-bn-u' read na-bu-u; XLII 48 'šar-ru-tiu' read šar-ru-tim.
- Stray marks taken as specks, not diacritics: colon-like hyphen in XLI 83 ap-ru-su and XLI 98 iš-ru-ku-šum; dot over the n of XLI 88 di-in-ši-na; tick after XLI 93 ni-ši-šu; mid-dot after XLII 1 ta-na-da-{b}tim and XLII 44 šu-ma-am; acute-like tick after XLII 51 li-iš-bi-ir; dots near XLI 100 '100' and XLII 43 a-wi-lu-tum.
- Epilogue page, no heading: all lines are carry. First printed text '-ru' completes XLII 56 la ut-ta-ka-ru, which is recorded on Cornell 122; this file starts at XLII 57.
- XLII 98: '{ilu}' stands at the end of one printed line and 'EN.KI' starts the next; joined as {ilu}EN.KI.
- Column XLII ends at line 103 (mu-ša-ri-ku) before 'COLUMN XLIII.'
- XLIII 25: brackets printed: li-iš-ḫi-[el]-zi.
- Numeral 45 is printed at the very end of the page after šu-pa-a-at; the text of XLIII 45 is on Cornell 126.
- Stray marks taken as specks: tick before XLII 58 šar-ru-ti-ia; mid-dot in XLII 69 la na-wa-ri-im; dot under XLII 78 šu-ub-ša-a-am; mid-dots after XLII 96 šar-ri-im and XLII 97 li-ša-aš-ki-in; odd hyphen shapes in XLIII 30 li-iš-ku-un-šum and XLIII 43 še-ri-zu; mark under li of XLIII 36 li-iz-zu-uḫ-šu; mid-dot before XLIII 42 ilum.
- COUNT MISMATCH XLIII 70–74: between numerals 70 and 75 there are only 4 bar-segments (i-na na-ak-bi-im | li-te-ir-šu | ma-zu i-na ḫu-ša-aḫ-ḫi-im | u bu-bu-tim). Numbered 70–73 and line 74 left absent; a bar is probably missing in Harper's print. Needs a human ruling.
- XLIII 83: printed 'mar+ri-eš-tu-um' with a plus-like sign (a cross) in place of the hyphen; copied as '+'. Could be a damaged hyphen.
- Column XLIII ends at line 106 (li-te-ir), and XLIV 1 is also li-te-ir.
- Stray marks taken as specks: tick under the bar after XLIII 78; colon-like hyphen in XLIII 82 gar-ra-du-um; mid-dot after XLIII 85 im-ni-ia; dot under a in XLIII 88 a-na; dot after XLIII 90 šu; specks near XLIII 98 palî-ia, XLIII 101 i-na, XLIII 103; dot over XLIV 2 taḫazim.
- XLIII 45: the raised b before ša is slightly damaged (looks like ь) but read as {b}.
- Epilogue continued; 'COLUMN XLII.' heading printed mid-page; col switches to XLII at line 1. Column XLI ends at line 105.
- XLII 5–9 (inferred): only four bar-separated units are visible before 10; split 'a-wa-ti-ia' / 'la uš-te-pi-el' (7/8) by analogy with XLII 29/30 on this page. The alternative is 'di-ni' / 'la u-{b}ša-az-zi-iḳ'. Needs a human check.
- XLII 20–21 and 50–51: 'ša i-na na-ru-ia' / 'aš-tu-ru' and 'ḫaṭṭi-šu' / 'li-iš-bi-ir' split at wide gaps (needed for the count).
- XLII 4: '{b}aš-' / 'tu-ru' joined across printed lines.
- XLII 28: 'up-ta-az-zi-is' — no caron visible on final s.
- XLII 55: the page ends mid-word 'ut-ta-ka-'; the rest of line 55 is on the next even page. Kept with its trailing hyphen.
- SCAN QUALITY: the top half of the page (XLII 56–79) is badly washed out. Hyphens show only as faint dots, and thin diacritics (carons on š, breves under ḫ) are often invisible where nearby forms in the same lines show them. I transcribed what is visible, so forms like mu-sar-bu-u, sar-ru-ti-ia, te-si, su-ub-, ha-la-ḳi-su, su-ub-ti-su, si-im-tim, li-ši-im-sum, sar-ru-zu, sum-šu, su-ub-sa-a-am and h for ḫ in ra-ah, ha-la-ḳi-su, {b}ha-aš-šum, ta-ne-hi-im, hu-sa-ah-hi-im, ha-la-aḳ (73) may have lost a caron or breve. Please check against a better copy.
- XLII 56 'ru' ends the stele line that starts at the foot of PDF p.126 ('la ut-ta-ka-'). The full line is la ut-ta-ka-ru; merge the two when assembling.
- Several dividers in the faint region are not visible, only wide gaps (e.g. li-iḳ-bi / {ilu}Bêlit / ummum; ki-be-za / i-na E.KUR; i-la-ka / abkal; šum-šu / mu-ša-ri-ku?). I treated wide gaps as dividers where the 5-line numerals require it. XLII 102–103: no divider is visible between 'mi-im-ma' (end of a printed row) and 'šum-šu', but there is a wide gap between 'šum-šu' and 'mu-ša-ri-ku', so I split it as 102 'mu-di mi-im-ma šum-šu' / 103 'mu-ša-ri-ku'. This is the last line of col. XLII, so the count can't be checked against a following numeral.
- XLII 62 'i-nà': the grave accent is clearly printed.
- XLII 65 'umi': no circumflex visible (cf. ûmi on p.130), possibly lost in the faint print.
- XLII 84 'E.KUR' has no accent here (p.132 prints É.KUR).
- XLIII 1 'û-um': circumflex faint but present.
- XLIII 4: a stray dot is printed just before 'li-te-ir-šu-ma'. I ignored it as a speck.
- XLIII 9 'li-iṣ-ki-ir': confirmed a dot under s on zoom. XLIII 20 '{b}li-is-ki-ip' has no dot.
- XLIII 35 'ba-al-tu-tim': no dot under the t on zoom; transcribed as printed.
- XLIII 18 'na-bi-iš-tim': caron clear in one strip, faint in another.
- Epilogue continues; no § heading, so laws is empty and all lines are in carry. The page continues XLIII from line 45 (p.128 ends with the numeral 45). 'COLUMN XLIV.' is a column header, not copied as a line. Lines between the 5-line numerals are counted from '|' dividers.
- SCAN QUALITY: the top third (XLIII 45–~72) is washed out, as on p.128. Carons and ḫ-breves are often invisible and hyphens faint. Forms transcribed as visible include sa/sar/su/se/si for possible ša/šar/šu/še/ši (lines 45, 46, 48, 49, 53, 56, 57, 58, 61, 63, 65, 68, 71) and h for possible ḫ (50 i-hal-li-ḳu, 52 arhi, 54 ta-ne-hi-im). Please check.
- XLIII 45 'agam kussâm {1}sa sar-ru-tim': I can't see a hyphen in 'agam' or 'kussâm' (they may be lost). The accent on kussâm is unclear (â or á). A raised '1' (a footnote reference) stands before 'sa'; it's recorded as {1}. I found no footnote text on this page.
- LINE COUNT PROBLEM (XLIII 51–54): the printed sequence is 'li-mu-zu-ma | ûmi arhi' [row end] 'arhi | sa na-a-at pali-su' [wide gap] 'i-na ta-ne-hi-im 55'. If the wide gap is a lost divider, the numbering forces 52 = 'ûmi arhi arhi' (no divider at the row break between the two arhi). If not, 52 'ûmi arhi', 53 'arhi', 54 'sa na-a-at pali-su i-na ta-ne-hi-im'. I chose the first. 'arhi' really is printed twice. 'sa na-a-at' may be ša-na-a-at with a lost hyphen.
- LINE JUMP XLIII 72→74: numerals 70 (before i-na na-ak-bi-im) and 75 (before li-ḫal-li-iḳ) enclose only four visible stele lines: li-te-ir-su | ma-zu i-na ḫu-ša-aḫ-ḫi-im | u bu-bu-tim. I numbered li-te-ir-su 71, 'ma-zu i-na ḫu-ša-aḫ-ḫi-im' 72 and 'u bu-bu-tim' 74, leaving no line 73. A divider is probably missing (perhaps between ma-zu and i-na), but none is visible, so I invented no line.
- XLIII 83 'mar-ri-eš-tu-um': the mark between 'mar' and 'ri' is a low blob, not a clean hyphen. Read as a hyphen.
- XLIII 98 'ra-i-ma-at': a small dot above the 'a' of 'ra'; probably a speck.

## Signs already in the shared sign glossary (signs-cuneiform.json) — key: values

- AN: an, diĝir (as det. {d}), Akkadian: Anum (the sky-god, the bare sign), ilum “god”
- NAM: Akkadian: nam
- LUGAL: Akkadian value šarrum “king”
- TA: ta
- E: e, e₃, è, Akkadian: e
- NE: ne, de₃, bil, dè — in A.GA.NE (Agade), bí
- A: Akkadian: a, A.ŠÀ = eqlum “field”, plural marker with ḪI (Harper reads ḪI+A as ZUN, §35)
- BA: Akkadian: ba
- NUN: nun, eridu (with KI), Akkadian: nun
- KI: ki 'place/earth', Akkadian: ki, qi₂; also the syllable ki in words
- LU: Akkadian: lu, second sign of SIPA “shepherd”, as logogram UDU — “sheep”, Akkadian immerum, lū “or; let …”, ṣēnum “sheep,
- LA: Akkadian: la
- GAR: ĝar, gar, qar — in qar-ra-dum “warrior”, GAR/NINDA — “bread, portion”, ŠA.GA (Harper) / NÍG.GA = makkūrum “property” (§6
- MU: Akkadian: mu, MU = šattum “year”: MU III{kam} “the third year” (§30)
- NI: ni, ì, Akkadian: ni, li₂, ì
- AK: ak, aĝ₂, aq
- IB: Akkadian: ib, ip, the god Uraš of Dilbat ({d}IB)
- BI: Akkadian: bi, bé, pi₂
- RU: ru, šub, Akkadian: ru
- DU: du, ĝen, gub, rá, DU — “to go, stand”
- EN: Akkadian: en; EN = bēlum “lord”; EN.LÍL = the god Enlil
- ME: Akkadian: me
- LU2: lù, lú, determinative before persons: {amēlu}agram “hireling” (§26, §33)
- NA: Akkadian: na
- GAL: GAL — “great”; GAL.GAL “the great (gods)”; GAL.BÚR = ušumgallum “dragon”; gál
- TUR: dumu, tur, as DUMU — “son”, Akkadian mārum, DUMU — mār “son”, DUMU+ti = mārtum “daughter” (§38–39)
- ZI: Akkadian: ṣi, ṣe
- PA: pa, sib (PA.LU), Akkadian: pa, PA.LU = SIPA “shepherd” (rēʾûm); PA.AL = šabra (in Mashkan-shabri), PA.PA — the captain (
- RA: Akkadian: ra
- URU: uru, eri, iri, Akkadian: ri₂ (in da-ri₂-tam “everlasting”), unu — Harper’s UNU.KI (Uruk) and UD.UNU.KI (Larsa); modern e
- ESZ: eš
- A2: Akkadian: id, it (ni-bi-it)
- IGI: igi, lim (in Alulim), Akkadian: ši; Sumerian igi “eye”
- EZENxBAD: in Dur-ilu{ki} (Der), “Fortress of the god”
- DUB: dub
- NAGAR: nagar, tibira, agru “hired man” — Harper’s own sign-list value; modern editions read the word as ḪUN.GÁ (§26, §33)
- ESH2: šè, šú
- UD: ud, u₄, Akkadian: ud, ut, tam; as logogram UTU = Šamaš, the sun-god, babbar — É.BABBAR.RA (Ebabbar, “Shining House”), ūm
- KIB: kib — the sign of UD.KIB.NUN (Sippar) and the Euphrates
- SU: su, SU — “flesh”
- KUR: kur, land, mountain, KUR — “mountain, land”; É.KUR = Ekur, Enlil’s temple, mat, šad
- DUR2: dúr, tuš
- MA: Akkadian: ma
- UR2: úr
- EGIR: egir
- DISH: 1 — I MA.NA “one mina” (§24)
- U: the numeral 10: adi 10-šu “tenfold” (§8)
- GESH2: 60
- GESHU: 600
- SHAR2: 3,600
- SHARU: 36,000
- SHARGAL: 216,000
- I: i
- BAD: be, bad, bat, til
- EL: el
- SHA: ša
- U3: ù (u₃) — the conjunction “and”
- IR: ir, er
- DIM: tim, dim, ṭim
- AD: ad, at, aṭ
- KALAM: KALAM — Sumerian “land”, read mātum in Akkadian, un
- AMAR: AMAR — “calf”; with UTU spells Marduk (AMAR.UTU, “calf of the Sun”)
- RI: ri, re, tal
- ESH: eš, 30 — three Winkelhaken, the numeral 30: adi 30-šu “thirtyfold” (§8)
- TI: ti, ṭi, TI — “arrow”, also “life” (Sumerian ti(l))
- IM: im, em, IM — also “clay, storm”, as logogram: {d}IM = Adad, the storm-god; {uru}IM{ki} = Karkar
- KISH: KIŠ — read kiššat “all, totality” in Akkadian (Harper’s sign list: ner, kiš, šēpu, kiššatu), ner (Harper) — {uru}NER.KI 
- TAG: šum, tag, tak, šum — in šum-ma “if”, the word that opens every law
- IN: in
- GI4: gi₄, ge₄
- U2: u₂ — the commonest writing of vowel u in Old Babylonian, Sumerian ú “plant”
- SAR: šar, SAR — Sumerian “garden / to write”, {giš}SAR (KIRI₆) = kirûm “orchard” (§27 on)
- SHU: šu, ŠU — “hand”, ŠU.ḪA = bāʾirum “fisher” (§26–41)
- KA2: KA₂ — “gate”; opens KA₂.DINGIR.RA “Babylon”, Bāb-ilim “gate of the god”, KÁ.GAL = abullum, the city gate (§15)
- TE: te, ṭe₄
- LI: li, le
- DA: da, ṭa
- HA: ḫa, ḪA — “fish”, second sign of ŠU.ḪA = bāʾirum “fisher”
- AM: am, AM — “wild bull” (GUD×KUR)
- AH: aḫ, eḫ, iḫ, uḫ, a’ — carries the glottal stop (ʾ) in words like na-a’-dam
- DAM: dam, DAM — “spouse”, DAM.GÀR = tamkārum “merchant” (§40), dam — “spouse”
- IA: ia (i+a ligature) — the sound y
- GA: ga, qa₂
- UL: ul
- HU: ḫu, MUŠEN — “bird” (as det.)
- KAL: dan — in dannum “strong”, kal, KAL — “mighty, precious”, LAMMA — the lamassu guardian spirit, dan — “strong”
- SAG: SAG — “head”; SAG.GI₆ “the black-headed” = mankind, sag
- MI: mi, gi₆ / gig₂ — “black, night”; second sign of SAG.GI₆
- PI: wa, wi, wu, pi — one sign for all the w-syllables
- TU: tu, ṭu₂
- UB: ub, up
- BU: bu, pu
- KU: ku, qu₂, KU — “to lie down”
- UR: ur, UR — “dog”
- NU: nu, Sumerian nu “not”, NU.TUR — the lieutenant (modern: laputtûm) §33–34
- UM: um
- KID: lil₂ — in {d}EN.LÍL “Enlil”, kid
- ISH: iš, Akkadian: iš, uš₅
- IGIGUNU: ši — the IGI sign with extra strokes (gunû); Harper writes ši(g), sig₇
- LUH: luḫ; ŠU.LUḪ = šuluḫḫu “purification-rites”
- ZU: zu, ZU — “to know”; in É.ZU.AB (E-abzu) and EN.ZU (Sin)
- AB: ab, ap, AB — “window”; in É.ZU.AB and ŠEŠ.AB (Ur)
- GISH: iz, is, iṣ, GIŠ — “wood, tree”; GIŠ.DAR = Ištar (old writing)
- IL2: íl — in É.SAG.ÍL.LA (Esagila)
- IL: il
- KUL: NUMUN — “seed”; Akkadian zērum (Harper: zêr, ZIR)
- SHESH: ŠEŠ — “brother”; opens ŠEŠ.AB (Ur)
- USH: uš, nit (Harper, in nit-ra-ru-šu), second sign of AGA₃.ÚS = rēdûm “soldier”, uš, nit
- GUM: qum, kum
- BIL: bil — the NE sign with extra strokes; in ba-bil “bringer”
- GAN: gan, ḫé — in ḪÉ.GÁL ḫegallum “abundance”; also the syllable in Da-gan
- SUHUSH: SUḪUŠ — “foundation”, Akkadian išdum (Harper: išid)
- GU: gu, {giš}GU.ZA = kussûm “chair, seat of office” (§5)
- MUSH3: {d}INANNA — the goddess Ishtar (Harper reads Nanâ), muš₃
- TUG2: dul₃ — in AN.DUL₃ ṣalūlum “protective canopy”, túg — “cloth, garment”
- TUM: tum, dum
- BUR2: búr — GAL.BÚR = ušumgallum, the dragon
- LUM: lum
- GA2: ma₃/mal — in {d}za-ma₃-ma₃ (Zamama) and MAL.KA.A (Malka/Malgium)
- HAR: ḫar/ḫur — in ḪAR.SAG.KALAM.MA (Hursag-kalama, “Mountain of the Land”)
- KISAL: KISAL — “courtyard”, Akkadian kisallum
- GU2: gú/tig — opens TIG.GAB.A (Cutha)
- GABA: gab — in TIG.GAB.A (Cutha), GABA — “breast”; modern editions read du₈ here
- SHID: šid — Harper’s ŠID.LAM (the Meslam) and É.MIŠ.MIŠ (Emishmish), modern reading: mes
- KA: KA — “mouth”; ina pī mātim “in the mouth of the land”, ka (syllable)
- AR: ar — the AR sign (IGI+RI)
- GIR2: gír, kir — in kir-bu-um (qerbum “within”); opens GIR.SU (Girsu)
- SHIR: šir — opens ŠIR.PUR.LA (Lagash)
- BUR: bur, pur — in ŠIR.PUR.LA (Lagash)
- NIN: NIN — “lady/lord”; in NIN.TU (Nintu) and NIN.A.ZU (Ninazu)
- DI: di, ṭi, DI — “judgment” (salīmum)
- GI: gi, GI — “reed”
- AL: al
- MASH: maš — in É.UL.MAŠ (Eulmash) and MAŠ.KAN (Mashkan-)
- GAN2: kan — in MAŠ.KAN.PA.AL (Mashkan-shabri), GAN₂ — “field”
- AZ: az — the lion-sign with ZA inside
- SI: si, SI — “horn”
- SA: sa
- SHE: še, ŠE — “barley, grain”
- IG: ig, ik, iq
- TAB: tab, TAB — “to double, twin”
